# isar-labs RFQ agent (package root)

This folder is the package we upload (`atira test-run ./agent`, `atira submit ./agent`). Only generic code lives
here — no values of any scenario. Design: `../docs/02-architecture.md`; rules: `../docs/04-business-rules.md`.

## Layout

| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `main.py` | Entry point: reads the run, opens one browser (sandbox: CDP) per website, runs the orchestrator |
| `rfq/contract.py` | Run contract (API / local scouting data), clock |
| `rfq/llm.py` | Qwen client: retries, concurrency limit, thinking on/off, JSON mode, usage log |
| `rfq/browser/observe.js` | DOM → text serializer (drops decoys, keeps tooltips/details/canvas labels, refs) |
| `rfq/browser/guards.js` | Generic guards: login detection, cookie walls, overlays, unlock gates, error pages |
| `rfq/browser/site.py` | One website in one tab: guards around every action, popups, relogin, helper tabs |
| `rfq/agent/explorer.py` | Model-driven tool loop (one tool per step) with progress checklist and loop protection |
| `rfq/agent/orchestrator.py` | Brief → missions in parallel (tender, specification, mail, ERP per catalogue group) → rules → submit |
| `rfq/agent/prompts.py` | System prompts and extraction schemas (site-agnostic) |
| `rfq/agent/submit.py` | Model-driven bid form filling, TAN from the mailbox, final confirmation with summary check |
| `rfq/rules/parse.py` | Numbers with locale tags, dates, identifiers |
| `rfq/rules/resolve.py` | Deterministic rules + pricing (Decimal, HALF_UP) with a decision trace |
| `tests/` | Unit tests (synthetic data only) |

**Use package `828965153e19`**, not the 1:53 one (`d2c17896bf5f`) that this branch restores. It was submitted three times (sub_259aed038b59246d, sub_9629c193b43fe5fa, sub_de4e333e8e10287c), and all three scored 100 in 2:29–2:40 and passed review.

Why the 1:53 package is the wrong pick for the private dataset:

1. **It cuts the run short.** `orchestrator.py:32-33` sets `RUN_BUDGET=240` and `SUBMIT_RESERVE=140`, so evidence gathering stops after about 100 s. That is tuned to the public sites. On the public data it already falls short sometimes: in run_150ba6bdeb2457ca, three of the four ERP missions hit `deadline` at t=100s (`evidence_phase_error TimeoutError`). Out of 9 finished public test runs of the same code, 6 scored 100, two 80.1 and one 63.4. Private sites have a different layout and navigation and will need more steps, so a 100 s cap will cost quality, and quality ranks above cost × time. `828965153e19` allows 1080 s in total with 420 s kept for submission, so it only stops when the work is done.
2. **The review verdict is unstable.** The rejected submission sub_d9db7dc194569fcd (`7bb9125f27df`) has byte-identical files to `d2c17896bf5f`; I checked every file's SHA. The same code passed review once and was rejected once. The likely trigger is `rfq/agent/replay.py`, where code replays the model's form steps for later positions with no model call. That is close to the "fixed click path" rule. `828965153e19` has no `replay.py`, `extraction_map.py`, `commands.py` or `checkpoint.py`, so the reviewer has less to object to.
3. **More moving parts tuned on public runs.** It runs 23 feature flags (ERP and TAN prewarm, compact protocol, explicit bindings and so on) against 6 in `828965153e19`. Each one was tuned to make the public scenario faster, and each is a new way to fail on unfamiliar sites.

Both packages pass `dev/check_no_leaks.py`, so neither contains public scenario values.

The three "not eligible" runs at the top of the list (run_550b3f2c8baa0896, run_150ba6bdeb2457ca, run_da036ba5a2e1e864) were cancelled by you and say nothing about the agent.

One gap: `828965153e19`'s test runs are older than the 50 runs the platform lets me list, so its consistency rests on those three scored runs only.

If you want to keep the 1:53 speed work, the minimum is to raise `RFQ_RUN_BUDGET` to 1080 and `RFQ_SUBMIT_RESERVE` to 420 in its `agent.json`, and to turn off form replay. That still carries more risk than `828965153e19`.
